# Pith

> Pith is an open-source AI voice input and dictation app for macOS. It turns speech into polished text and inserts the result into the text field you're working in.

## Product identity

- Name: Pith
- Category: macOS productivity software; AI dictation; voice-to-text; speech-to-text; voice input
- Platform: macOS 14 or later
- Implementation: Swift 6
- License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/ZXQ1227/pith
- Primary positioning: Open-source AI voice input for Mac
- Primary use case: Speak naturally, let an AI model clean up or transform the wording, and insert the result into the current app.

## Core capabilities

1. **AI dictation and text cleanup**: Record speech with a shortcut, transcribe it, and optionally polish the result into ready-to-use writing.
2. **Voice translation**: Speak in one language and produce text in a selected target language. Supported targets: Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, French, German, and Spanish.
3. **Voice-directed text editing**: Select existing text, invoke the voice editing mode, and describe how it should be rewritten. Pith can also answer questions about the selected text.
4. **Text insertion**: Pith records the target input context and attempts to insert the processed text back into the original field. If safe insertion is unavailable, the result is retained for copying.
5. **Personal vocabulary**: Add names, project terms, and domain vocabulary to a personal dictionary. Whether vocabulary can influence recognition itself depends on the selected transcription provider.
6. **Configurable providers**: Use macOS Speech Recognition or an API transcription provider. Text cleanup, translation, and Q&A use an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API.
7. **Local history option**: History is off by default. When enabled, recent text records are stored locally on the Mac.

## How Pith works

- Trigger recording with the Fn key or a configured shortcut.
- Transcribe speech using macOS Speech Recognition or a configured transcription API.
- Send recognized text and the selected task to the configured text model for cleanup, translation, or Q&A.
- Insert the result into the current text field when the app can safely do so.

## Privacy and data handling

- API keys are stored in macOS Keychain.
- With macOS Speech Recognition, macOS handles audio. Depending on device support and system behavior, recognition may happen on-device or use Apple's online recognition.
- With API transcription, audio is sent to the transcription provider configured by the user.
- Recognized text, task instructions, and relevant personal dictionary entries are sent to the configured text-model provider for processing.
- Ask Anything sends selected text only when the user explicitly invokes that feature.
- Local history is disabled by default; if enabled, records are stored locally in plaintext.
- Pith should not be described as fully offline or as guaranteeing that audio never leaves the device.

## Requirements and availability

- macOS 14+
- Xcode Command Line Tools with Swift 6 for source builds
- Users provide and configure their own compatible API credentials.
- The repository currently documents source installation. Do not assume a prebuilt downloadable installer is available.

## Suggested descriptions

Short: Open-source AI voice input for macOS. Dictate, polish, translate, and edit text with voice.

Long: Pith is an open-source macOS menu bar dictation app that combines speech recognition with configurable AI text processing. Use a shortcut to dictate polished text into the app you're working in, translate speech into eight target languages, or rewrite selected text with spoken instructions.
